A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MetaGFN work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on the line, two-dimensional grid, and alanine-dipeptide environments, including repeated training runs and supplementary analyses in Appendices E–G.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments across five environments, additional baseline comparisons, and a new hyperparameter sensitivity study in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The KDE-based Adapted Metadynamics procedure and MetaGFN's backward sampling, replay, and on-policy training remain unchanged. v2's Algorithm 2 matches v1's Appendix D Algorithm 3; regenerating trajectories was already the variant used in v1's main experiments.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from three environments to five through new three- and four-dimensional grids with eight and sixteen modes. The retained two-dimensional grid also changes its mode coordinates from ±7 to ±10. The line and alanine-dipeptide environments remain.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates on-policy training, noisy exploration, and Thompson sampling. v2 Figure 5 adds Local Search GFlowNets to the comparisons and nested sampling to alanine dipeptide and the grid environments. Nested sampling is explicitly excluded from the line experiment.

E3.justification: Grid batch size changes from 64 to 128. New higher-dimensional experiments use longer trajectories, two-component policies, and coarser metadynamics grids. v2 also reports a common replay admission threshold of 10^-3, replacing v1's grid and alanine-specific thresholds of 10^-4 and 10^-10. These are reported setting revisions, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 and Figure 8 add a line-environment sensitivity study varying replay-buffer and metadynamics frequencies. The earlier trajectory-regeneration/noise ablations, KDE exploration analysis, and alanine best/worst-run cases are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The main comparisons retain means and standard-error bands over ten repeats. v2 removes v1's conflicting prose describing these bands as standard deviations and explicitly reports standard deviations over ten repeats for the new sensitivity plot. No increase in repeats for existing experiments or new significance testing is established.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 5 adds baseline and higher-dimensional results and revises the two-dimensional grid curves under changed settings. New findings include nested sampling outperforming MetaGFN on the three-dimensional grid with DB loss, while Figure 8 favors replay frequency 2. Alanine mode counts in Table 1 remain identical. Revised grid curves do not establish same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: Definition 2.1(iv) adds an explicit requirement that reaching the sink be guaranteed within a bounded number of steps. Theorem 3.1, the appendix lemmas, and the core convergence argument are retained; most proof edits concern indices and coordinate notation.

C1.justification: The central algorithmic and consistency contributions remain. v2 narrows the introduction's claim of absent continuous-exploration benchmarking to limited prior literature and adds explicit claims of no pre-training and small, constant cost per training trajectory.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking poorer higher-dimensional performance to reduced replay diversity, contrasts refreshed MetaGFN samples with fixed nested-sampling samples, and explains replay-frequency tradeoffs. The dependence on suitable low-dimensional collective variables and the alanine convergence failure case remain acknowledged.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the code placeholder with a specific MetaGFN repository address and supplies a nested-sampling implementation address. It adds Local Search reconstruction settings and higher-dimensional policy and grid-resolution details. Most existing implementation, hardware, and training-time information is retained and consolidated.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially develops positioning against Sendera et al.'s off-policy diffusion-sampler training and gradient-based MCMC approaches. New references and discussion cover nested sampling, local credit assignment, and collective-variable learning methods. This changes the account of related research beyond bibliography formatting.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the exploration and collective-variable background, divides the method into dedicated subsections, and separates environment descriptions from results. Experimental appendices are reorganized into one Appendix D with common settings, while algorithm descriptions are integrated into their relevant sections.

P2.justification: v2 adds a metadynamics schematic and sensitivity plot, combines three separate performance figures into an expanded fifteen-panel Figure 5, and relocates the MetaGFN pseudocode into the main text. The paired alanine energy/KDE display is split between the main text and appendix, alongside extensive layout and typography changes.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited comparative evaluation through two additional exploration baselines, harder grid environments, and a frequency sensitivity study. These results better establish both MetaGFN's advantages and its dimensionality limitations. Stronger research positioning and concrete code-access information further improve the paper, although the core theoretical argument remains largely unchanged.
